item.title: Delta attack: PANDEF writes IGP, DSS DG, demands probe
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has written to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Ajayi, demanding an urgent investigation into the reported violence at a political rally in Ughelli, Delta State. The socio-political organisation called on both security chiefs to work with other relevant agencies to identify and prosecute those who allegedly planned, sponsored, instigated or participated in the attack on the campaign train of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Omo-Agege, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Delta Central, was reportedly attacked during a campaign rally on Monday, November 23, 2026, with some persons said to have been killed and several others injured. In a letter signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, PANDEF strongly condemned the incident and described the reported loss of lives and injuries as disturbing and unacceptable. The organisation also urged the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to provide financial and other forms of assistance to families of those reportedly killed, as well as adequate medical care for the injured. In the letter, PANDEF said it was shocked by reports of violence at a political rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in parts of Uduere, Delta State, on Monday. It, however, noted that the reports of deaths and injuries had yet to be officially corroborated. “According to media reports, which are yet to be officially corroborated, some persons reportedly lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. We consider these reported incidents extremely disturbing and totally unacceptable,” the letter stated. PANDEF recalled that it had issued a statement the previous week warning against political violence, intimidation and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South. It said the latest incident, coming days after its appeal, was a source of grave concern, adding that the region had traditionally upheld political tolerance, sportsmanship and civility. The organisation further warned that insecurity in the South-South could have implications beyond the region, given its strategic importance to Nigeria’s oil and gas industry and national economy. “Any disruption of peace and security in the region, particularly violence associated with political and electoral activities, could have far-reaching implications, not only for the safety and wellbeing of our people but also for the stability and economic survival of the country,” it said. PANDEF urged the police, DSS and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive, impartial and thorough investigation and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice in accordance with the law. item.title: Tinubu willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists — Bwala
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Special Adviser to the President on Media and Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has said President Bola Tinubu is willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists, while maintaining that the Presidency will decide which media organisations interview him. Bwala said this during an interview on the Niger Unfiltered podcast, published on Thursday, following questions about why Tinubu had granted only one official interview to Nigerian media organisations in about three years and seven months in office. “I expect us to do more. And the second time, you’ll see more of that,” Bwala said. He acknowledged that some interviews had been postponed at short notice, saying the President had sometimes agreed to meet journalists before later rescheduling. “There are a number of times in which the President called for media. At the 11th hour, he may have been advised, and then he would apologise and say some other time,” Bwala said. The presidential aide said Tinubu was willing to speak with journalists and did not need prepared answers or prior briefings before interviews. “There is a willingness to grant interviews on the part of the President. And the President, when granting interviews, didn’t need to read anything, didn’t need to be briefed,” he said. Bwala defended the Presidency’s right to choose the journalists and platforms it engages, saying it should not be pressured to grant interviews to specific media organisations. “We control our narrative. We decide who we grant interviews to. Nobody can come and tell us, grant to this one and not the other one,” he said. He said State House press corps members representing mainstream, new, social and print media covered the President’s daily activities. “In the State House press corps, we have representatives of the mainstream, the new media, the social media, and the print media. So every day, the activity of the President is covered by them,” Bwala said. He also criticised some media practitioners over what he described as political bias and a lack of professionalism, arguing that Tinubu should engage journalists capable of conducting balanced interviews. Bwala’s remarks followed criticism of Tinubu’s recent interview with American political strategist and media personality Diana London. Some Nigerians questioned why the President had granted an interview to a foreign media personality while rarely speaking with Nigerian journalists. The controversy grew after reports linked London to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving a United States-based firm engaged by the Nigerian government. London denied receiving the money from the Federal Government or anyone in Nigeria, saying she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also challenged Tinubu to grant a live interview to Nigerian journalists and called for the release of the full, unedited recording of his conversation with London. item.title: FCCPC urges supermarkets to protect consumer trust
item.description: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has urged supermarket and shopping mall operators across the country to strengthen consumer protection practices and earn customers’ trust through transparent business operations. The Executive Vice Chairman of the commission, Mr Tunji Bello, gave the advice through the Lagos Zonal Coordinator, Dr Olubunmi Otti, at a one-day sectoral roundtable on compliance and enforcement of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA) 2018, held in Lagos. The engagement, themed, “Compliance Obligations of Supermarket Operators,” was organised to sensitise operators on their responsibilities under the law, particularly as the yuletide shopping season approaches. Bello said supermarkets had become essential to millions of Nigerians, serving as major outlets for purchasing food, medicines, children’s necessities and other household essentials. He said customers placed their health, money and trust in the hands of supermarket operators whenever they patronised their businesses, adding that such trust must be protected. “The supermarket is no longer just a shop for millions of Nigerians; it is where they buy their food, medicine, children’s needs and daily essentials. “When a consumer walks into your store, they are placing their trust, their health and hard-earned money in your hands. That trust must be protected,” he said. The FCCPC boss said the FCCPA 2018 empowered the commission to protect consumers, promote fair competition and ensure that businesses operated transparently and accountably. He said the roundtable focused on the commission’s role in guiding compliance, consumer rights under the Act, safety standards in retail outlets, the legal framework and complaint resolution mechanisms. Bello disclosed that the commission received complaints daily concerning the supermarket sector, including discrepancies between shelf prices and prices charged at checkout points, the sale of expired or nearly expired products without clear disclosure, misleading promotions and discounts, poor refund and return policies, and inadequate product information. He cited the experience of a mother who budgeted N50,000 for monthly shopping but encountered higher prices at the payment counter, describing such discrepancies as a breach of consumer trust rather than a mere mistake. He said the commission’s objective was to reduce and ultimately eliminate such complaints, not to shut down businesses, but to help operators understand and comply with their obligations. “Compliance is not a burden; compliance is good business,” he said, adding that customers who trusted a supermarket’s products and refund policies were more likely to return. The engagement attracted representatives of supermarket and retail businesses, including Justrite Superstores, Jendol Superstores, Prince Ebeano Supermarkets, Sundry Foods and Edichat Pharmacy and Stores. item.title: Igbokoda crash: Tinubu approves N100m, three-bedroom houses for victims’ families
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi President Bola Tinubu has approved three-bedroom flats in Abuja for the families of the 25 people who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. He also announced the award of the sum of N100 million to the families of each military personnel who died in the crash, separate from the houses. The President made the announcement on Thursday during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony held in honour of the victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. He said the houses, located in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja, would be allocated to the immediate families of the deceased military personnel and civilians who were aboard the aircraft. Tinubu described the housing allocation as a demonstration of the nation’s appreciation for the sacrifices of the fallen personnel. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of three-bedroom flats in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. “No home can ever replace the one you have lost, but they gave their lives for Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their family a home,” he said. The president pointed out that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft. “In addition to the flats, these officers would receive from this government N100m each,” he said. He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony. “Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen,” Tinubu said. The president also assured Nigerians that the October 5 aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. “We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said. Tinubu further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the welfare, safety and operational capacity of the Armed Forces through modernisation, training and better equipment. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wings it can build,” he added. The president urged the bereaved families to remember the deceased for their service and contributions to the country, assuring them that their sacrifices would remain in the nation’s memory. The October 5 accident claimed the lives of 25 people, including military personnel and civilians. item.title: Kwara Jailbreak: How negligence, insecurity aided inmates’ escape from 112-year-old Ilorin prison
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The jailbreak at the Correctional Centre, Oke-Kura, Ilorin, Kwara State, in the wee hours of last week Wednesday (November 18, 2026) exposed negligence, compromise of the staff and obsolete security equipment, according to Vanguard investigations. Sources at the centre confided in Vanguard that seven condemned prison inmates actually planned their escape, out of which two – Segun and Abraham – now declared wanted, were lucky. They had been planning their escape for about seven months. The rooms of the condemned prison inmates are said to be secluded and often dark, as they’re not supposed to go out like others. Vanguard also gathered that once in a while, when the condemned inmates go out to do social services, they are always heavily guarded. It was further gathered that for the seven months, they used a chisel to gradually opened the wall of their room, to create enough hole space for them to escape into the premises. Vanguard also gathered that they used posters to cover the space (inside and outside) so that no staff could easily notice their escape plan. It was further gathered that the Correctional Centre fence, about 17 feet high, was topped with embedded broken glass rather than a wire mesh. Furthermore, there is no CCTV camera covering inmates’ movements. D-Day On the day of escape, they got thick blankets which they tied together to make a long thick rope, and hooked it to the broken glasses on top of the fence. It was with this blanket-rope that the condemned inmates climbed over the tall fence and escaped to the other side, said a source. But after Segun and Abraham had scaled the fence, the blanket became weak. So it gave way, and the other five would-be escapees fell back on the prison premises. Vanguard also gathered that fully armed officers of the center, who were supposed to be on 24/7 surveillance to secure the other side of the fence, weren’t there to arrest the condemned inmates. It was during the morning roll call on Wednesday that the Correctional Centre staff on duty discovered that two condemned inmates had escaped. Overcrowding, staffing, infrastructure, management of prisons The Correctional Centre, Ilorin was constructed by the colonial master in 1914, about 110 years ago and lack updated facilities Vanguard reliably gathered. So, the facilities are strong, but grossly outdated. Vanguard further gathered that the challenge of overcrowding is prevalent in the centre. For instance, the centre was constructed in 1914 to accommodate 150 inmates but currently houses over 1,000. Vanguard further gathered that the staff in Ilorin Correctional Centre do not also match up with the overcrowded inmates. Of particular note is the lack of CCTV cameras to provide effective surveillance on the inmates, which also confirmed lack of security, and intelligent failures of the authorities. item.title: ‘I bought book on how to have boy-child’ – Makinde
item.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. That was what produced the boy, and I was finally left off the hook,” he said. Vanguard News The post ‘I bought book on how to have boy-child’ – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people . The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away. The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability. The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars. Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared. “We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster. “Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. item.title: Why Niniola and I have never released a song together – Teni
item.description: Nigerian singer Teni has explained why she and her elder sister, fellow music star Niniola, have yet to release a song together despite their individual successes in the music industry. The singer made the revelation during a question and answer session on Tea with Taylor , hosted by actor Taymesan Emmanuel. Comedian Bovi, who was among the audience, asked Teni why the sisters had never collaborated on a song, prompting her to explain that their conversations rarely revolve around music. According to her, whenever they meet or speak, they spend most of their time chatting and discussing other matters rather than working on music. “We are just two crazy girls. We will just be doing amebo and gisting all the time, forgetting to make music,” she said. She added that music hardly comes up whenever they speak, but suggested that fans could finally get the long-awaited collaboration in 2027. “I kid you not, every time Nini and I talk, we never talk about music. I know it’s bad. We are going to give you guys come 2027,” Teni said. The singer’s comments have renewed anticipation among fans for a joint project from the sisters, whose careers have developed independently within the Nigerian music industry. Teni, whose full name is Teniola Apata, gained prominence with songs such as Uyo Meyo and Case , while Niniola, born Niniola Apata, established herself with popular tracks including Maradona and Bana . Both singers have earned recognition for their distinct musical styles, with Teni known for her playful delivery and Niniola celebrated for her blend of Afro-house and other contemporary African sounds. Although they have not released a joint song, Teni’s latest remarks suggest that a collaboration could be on the way in 2027. item.title: Anambra: Pregnant woman delivers after APLUC seals building
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A nine-month pregnant woman, Mrs Nkechi Theophlus, has delivered her baby after reportedly collapsing following the sealing of her residential building by officials of the Anambra State Property and Land Use Charge (APLUC) in Obosi, Idemili North Local Government Area of the state. The woman reportedly went into labour and delivered her baby in the early hours of Thursday after being rushed to a hospital following the incident. The incident occurred at No. 1 Anyeji Omenwa Street, Obosi, where the officials allegedly padlocked the main entrance to the compound and sealed the building with red tape. The sealing reportedly left the landlady, Prophetess Ukamaka Lauretta Okafor, tenants and other occupants of the three-storey building, comprising 11 flats and rooms in the boys’ quarters, unable to gain access to their homes. The landlady, who protested the action, accused APLUC officials of refusing to issue her a receipt for the N120,000 she allegedly paid to the agency in February, while demanding additional payments. Addressing journalists on Thursday, Okafor said she was not indebted to the agency, insisting that the officials had failed to provide evidence of the full payment she made. She alleged that although N120,000 was deducted from her account through the officials’ Point of Sale (POS) machine, she was issued a receipt for only N90,000. According to her, the officials promised to provide a receipt for the outstanding N30,000 at their office but failed to do so despite her repeated visits. She said she was subsequently informed that the N120,000 payment covered her 2024 liability, while further payments were required for 2025 and 2026. Okafor said she expressed willingness to settle the outstanding payments but insisted that she must first receive evidence of the previous payment. She alleged that the officials refused to issue receipts or a covering note for subsequent payments, instead asking her to pay cash or surrender her ATM card for transactions through their POS machine. She said: “As I am speaking with you now, the N120,000 I paid in February this year, they have not given me the receipt. “I now told them that I will not continue to pay money that won’t be receipted or any evidence of payment given to me. I even told them to give me a covering note for me to pay all the money they are demanding, that I am ready at any moment to pay all the money they are demanding, but they insisted they won’t give me any receipt or covering note.” The landlady also alleged that the enforcement exercise was carried out without prior notice to her or other occupants of the building. She said the sealing left children returning from school and other tenants stranded outside their homes, with some forced to spend the night outdoors. item.title: Full list as CAF shortlist 5 for Women’s Player of the Year award
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled five finalists for the 2026 Women’s Player of the Year award, with Malawi sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga leading a shortlist featuring some of the continent’s outstanding footballers. Cameroon’s Monique Ngock, Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Morocco’s Hanane Aït El Haj complete the five-player list for African women’s football’s highest individual honour. The finalists were selected from an initial shortlist of 10 nominees based on their performances for club and country during the year. The shortlist reflects an eventful year for women’s football in Africa, highlighted by Cameroon’s historic triumph at the TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) Morocco 2026 and Malawi’s remarkable run to the final on their tournament debut. The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, on Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. 5 finalists for CAF Women’s Player of the Year 2026 1. Monique Ngock (Cameroon / Washington Spirit) Cameroon’s Monique Ngock earned a place among the finalists following her influential performances in helping the Indomitable Lionesses win their first WAFCON title at the 2026 tournament in Morocco. The midfielder was named Best Player of the Tournament after playing a key role in Cameroon’s historic campaign, which ended with a 3-0 victory over Malawi in the final in Rabat. Her commanding displays, technical ability and leadership in midfield also earned her a place in CAF’s official Team of the Tournament. Her contributions to the national team, alongside her performances for US club Washington Spirit, have strengthened her reputation as one of Africa’s leading midfielders. 2. Temwa Chawinga (Malawi / Kansas City Current) Temwa Chawinga enjoyed an outstanding year, helping Malawi reach the WAFCON 2026 final on their tournament debut and secure historic qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The forward won the Golden Boot at the tournament after scoring five goals and providing two assists. She finished level on goals with Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Cameroon’s Marie Ngah Manga but claimed the award on the strength of her assists. Temwa’s performances also earned her a place in CAF’s Team of the Tournament. 3. Tabitha Chawinga (Malawi / OL Lyonnes) Tabitha Chawinga joins her younger sister Temwa on the final shortlist after playing an important role in Malawi’s impressive campaign at WAFCON 2026. The OL Lyonnes forward brought experience, creativity and goalscoring quality to the Malawian side as they defied expectations to reach the final. item.title: Ebonyi NDC deputy gov candidate defects to APC; declares support for Tinubu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Ambassador Uka Chris Ndubuisi, has defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC), declaring support for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Francis Nwifuru. Ndubuisi announced his decision at the APC governorship campaign rally in Ebonyi State on Thursday, saying he had chosen to leave the NDC and collapse the party’s structure in the state. “My name is Ambassador Uka Chris Ndubuisi, and I am the Deputy Governorship candidate of NDC, and also the NDC Youth National Publicity Secretary. “No two ways. I just want to make this declaration that I have decided. Nobody forced me to it; on my own, I have decided to give my support to Mr President Bola Tinubu and our beloved Governor, His Excellency Francis Nwifuru. From today, we are collapsing the structure of NDC in Ebonyi State,” he said. Ndubuisi was received by Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Former governor and Minister of Works, David Umahi and APC supporters in the state. Umahi presented him to the party chairman, who was to formally hand him over to Nwifuru, the party’s leader in the state. According to INEC, Ndubuisi was listed as the running mate to NDC governorship candidate Senator Paulinus Igwe Nwagu for the February 6, 2027 election. The ticket was set to challenge incumbent Governor Francis Nwifuru and his deputy, Patricia Obila, who are seeking re-election on the APC platform. item.title: Nobody will love us the way Tinubu loves us in Ebonyi — Gov Nwifuru
item.description: Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has urged residents to vote for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying the president has demonstrated love for the state through projects and deserves overwhelming support in return. Nwifuru said Ebonyi residents should repay Tinubu’s gesture by delivering 100 per cent of their votes to him in the next presidential election. The governor spoke on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress governorship campaign, where he said he was more concerned about mobilising support for Tinubu than campaigning for himself. “The president has given us a project that nobody ever envisaged we will have, and to pay back is to vote for Mr President 100 per cent,” he said. Nwifuru said the state’s political leadership had promised Tinubu 1.3 million votes, expressing confidence that residents would fulfil the pledge. “Our leader said we are promising him 1.3 million votes. I want to tell you, I’m not here to campaign for myself. I am here to campaign for our dear president,” the governor said. He urged the people to acknowledge the projects and interventions the president had brought to Ebonyi, saying the benefits were visible and should not be overlooked. According to him, the Minister of Works had already outlined the projects executed or being undertaken in the state, adding that residents should take the message to their communities. Nwifuru insisted that Tinubu’s commitment to Ebonyi was unmatched, urging residents to demonstrate their appreciation through their votes. “You refused to see what he’s done, and it’s something that is very practical. The Honourable Minister of Works has enumerated it, you’ve heard from him, but I want you to take this message home,” he said. “No other person will love us the way President Bola Ahmed Tinubu loves us, and it’s a payback time,” the governor added. item.title: 74 Killed In Niger Communal Clash, Bago Orders Investigation, Donates N148m To Families
item.description: The clash between Kambari vigilantes and Fulani herders in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State resulted in the death of 74 persons. The state’s governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, disclosed this during a visit to the Emir of Borgu, Alhaji Halilu Sani Dantoro, at his palace in New Bussa, the LGA’s headquarters. Terrorists had, last Saturday, attacked Lumman-Ba’are community in Borgu LGA, killing the village head, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, his wife and three of his children. They also set his palace ablaze. Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, has ordered a thorough investigation into the clashes.‎ ‎The governor commiserated with the traditional ruler and people of the kingdom over the tragic incident. ‎Bago said the investigation was aimed at identifying those responsible for the violence and uncovering the remote and immediate causes of the recurring communal conflicts, with a view to preventing future occurrences. ‎He called on residents of the affected communities to embrace peaceful coexistence, tolerance and mutual understanding, stressing that no meaningful development could take place in an atmosphere of violence and hostility. ‎The governor expressed sympathy with the families of the victims and announced a donation of ₦2 million to each of the 74 affected families, amounting to ₦148 million, alongside the provision of foodstuffs and building materials to support those whose houses were destroyed during the clashes. ‎He commended the Borgu Emirate Council for its continued efforts towards maintaining peace and unity among the people, while urging Nigerians to learn to live together irrespective of their differences. ‎In his response, the Emir of Borgu, Muhammad Haliru -Dantoro Kitoro IV, appreciated the governor for the condolence visit and the timely deployment of security personnel to the area. ‎The traditional ruler acknowledged the state government’s efforts in deploying joint tactical security teams to tackle security challenges, including insurgency, in the area. He, however, expressed sadness that some individuals had chosen to resort to violence despite ongoing efforts by the government and security agencies to restore lasting peace. ‎The Emir also commended security agencies for their swift response, which he said helped to contain the situation and restore normalcy to the affected communities. ‎In his remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi, commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his efforts towards addressing security challenges across the country, noting that the restructuring of the nation’s security architecture was yielding positive results. ‎He also praised Governor Bago for his commitment to tackling insecurity in parts of Niger State and acknowledged the contributions of security agencies in containing threats to lives and property. ‎The governor was accompanied on the visit by the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi; Member representing Borgu/Agwara Federal Cons

item.title: FG issues strong advisory on harmattan fires, flags off safety campaign
item.description: …Warns against attacks on firefighters, careless fuel storage By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has issued a strong advisory on the risk of fire during the harmattan season, urging Nigerians to avoid overloading electrical sockets, leaving cooking unattended, burning refuse indiscriminately and storing petrol carelessly. The Controller General of the Federal Fire Service FFS, Samuel Adeyemi Olumode, gave the advisory on Thursday while flagging off the 2026 Harmattan Fire Safety Campaign. The campaign will run through February 2027. He spoke via a virtual fire chat on “The Roles and Responsibilities of Stakeholders in Building a Fire Safety-Resilient Community.” “The Harmattan period comes with dry and dusty weather conditions, low humidity and dry vegetation, all of which can contribute to the rapid spread of fire. “Activities involving cooking, electrical appliances, generators, gas cylinders, fuel storage and open burning require greater caution during this period”, he said. He advised households to “regularly inspect gas cylinders, hoses and connections, and ensure that generators are operated in properly ventilated outdoor spaces.” Parents and guardians, he said, “must also keep matches, lighters and other ignition sources away from children.” Olumode also warned business owners, market operators, school administrators, event organisers and managers of public facilities to put proper fire safety arrangements in place. “Prevention should never be treated as an expense that can be postponed until an emergency occurs,” he said. The Controller General condemned a recent attack on firefighters who were attacked at 7th Avenue, Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Friday, 13th November 2026. “At about 10am, firefighters from the Kubwa Metropolitan Fire Station, who had responded to a distress call, were attacked by suspected hoodlums who pelted them with stones. One of our personnel sustained a head injury and required medical attention. “Let me state clearly that attacks on firefighters will not be tolerated,” Olumode declared, adding that the suspected perpetrators had been apprehended. “Let me assure Nigerians that this matter will not be treated lightly. The appropriate authorities will ensure that those found culpable face the full weight of the law. There must be no justification for violence against emergency responders”, he said. The CGF said no emergency response system could function effectively “when firefighters are attacked, obstructed or prevented from carrying out their duties.” Olumode linked the safety of responders to the Service’s 15-minute response-time target. item.title: WhatsApp to allow users schedule messages – here’s how you can
item.description: WhatsApp has introduced a scheduled messaging feature that allows users to compose messages in advance and choose when they should be delivered, addressing one of the most requested additions to the messaging platform. The feature will enable users to schedule messages between 10 minutes and 14 days ahead in both individual and group chats. Announcing the update, WhatsApp said the feature would allow users to write messages when they think of them and have them delivered at a more appropriate time. “That’s why we’re introducing scheduled messages – one of our most requested features. You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats,” the company said. According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages will appear in recipients’ chats like ordinary messages, without any indication that they were composed and scheduled earlier. Users will also be able to view all their scheduled messages and delete them before delivery if they change their minds. How to schedule messages on WhatsApp To schedule a message on WhatsApp, users can follow these steps: Open WhatsApp and select an individual or group chat. Type the message they want to send. Press and hold the send button. Select the preferred date and time for the message to be delivered. Confirm the schedule. The message will then be delivered automatically at the selected time. WhatsApp said scheduled messages would still be delivered even if the sender’s phone was switched off or ran out of battery. The feature will support text messages, photographs and videos, giving users the option to plan different types of communication ahead of time. The company also assured users that scheduled messages would retain WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption, meaning only the sender and intended recipients would be able to read them. “Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us,” WhatsApp said. The scheduled messaging feature is rolling out globally over the coming weeks, although the company did not specify when it would become available to all users. WhatsApp said the update was another way for users to stay connected with important people by ensuring their messages arrive at exactly the right time. Vanguard News The post WhatsApp to allow users schedule messages – here’s how you can appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria’s trade hits ₦41.4tn in Q2 as NPA records 24.8% cargo growth
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s expanding trade activities are increasingly highlighting the strategic importance of the maritime sector, with cargo volumes handled across the nation’s seaports recording significant growth amid rising merchandise trade. The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) disclosed that cargo throughput across Nigerian ports rose by 24.8 per cent, from 103.6 million metric tonnes in 2024 to 129.3 million metric tonnes in 2025, indicating increased port utilisation and growing cargo-handling activities. The growth momentum extended into the first half of 2026, as cargo throughput increased by 12.2 per cent to 68.2 million metric tonnes, compared with 60.8 million metric tonnes recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The development comes against the backdrop of Nigeria’s merchandise trade rising to ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, further highlighting the critical role of ports in facilitating international trade, cargo movement and broader economic activities. Speaking at a two-day data-driven business and maritime reporting training organised in partnership with the Premium Times Training Academy in Ikeja, Lagos, on Wednesday, the General Manager, Corporate Affairs Division, NPA, Mr Ikechukwu Onyemekara, urged journalists to embrace evidence-based journalism, saying accurate maritime reporting was critical to trade, investment decisions and public understanding of the economy. He said Nigeria’s merchandise trade value of ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, representing a 5.6 per cent increase over the corresponding period of 2025, demonstrated the scale of economic activity linked to the movement of cargo through the country’s ports. According to him, port efficiency has far-reaching implications for manufacturers, exporters, importers, consumers and investors, as delays and operational bottlenecks ultimately increase the cost of doing business and affect the prices of goods. Onyemekara said the country’s ports received 2,300 ships in the first half of 2026, compared with 2,152 vessels in the same period of 2025, while outward cargo accounted for 41.9 per cent of total throughput in the second quarter, indicating improved export activity. He urged maritime journalists to look beyond headline figures and examine the factors driving growth, citing Lekki Deep Sea Port, which handled nearly 40 per cent of cargo throughput across Nigerian ports in the first half of 2026. He said more than three-quarters of Lekki’s cargo traffic was linked to refinery operations, stressing that a breakdown of the figures was necessary to understand how industrial investments were reshaping port activities and trade flows. On the NPA’s reform efforts, Onyemekara said the authority was pursuing port modernisation, digitalisation, export facilitation and sustainability initiatives to improve efficiency and competitiveness. item.title: Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations
item.description: ‎Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, has received the report of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry established to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 artisanal miners while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger State Command. ‎The Governor received the report from the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, at the Government House, Minna, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to implementing its recommendations. ‎Governor Bago expressed appreciation to the Commission on behalf of the bereaved families, the Miners Association and the NSCDC, describing the report as an important document that would guide stakeholders in addressing the circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. ‎He commended Justice Muhammad and members of the Commission for their dedication, sacrifices and thoroughness throughout the investigation, assuring that the government would carefully consider the findings and recommendations. ‎The Governor also disclosed that a copy of the report would be forwarded to the Presidency for reference, underscoring the importance of the investigation and its outcome. ‎Earlier, the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, thanked the Governor for the confidence reposed in the panel and the opportunity to serve. ‎He explained that the Commission received nine memoranda, conducted public hearings and carried out inspection visits to two mining sites, two NSCDC offices and the General Hospital in Minna as part of its investigation. ‎Justice Muhammad said the evidence and facts gathered during the proceedings formed the basis of the Commission’s findings and recommendations. ‎He further explained that the report was presented in three volumes for ease of reference, with Volume One containing the findings, observations and recommendations; Volume Two containing the records of proceedings; and Volume Three comprising all exhibits tendered before the Commission. ‎In his remarks, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Nasiru Mu’azu, described the deaths of the 37 artisanal miners as a grave incident in the history of Niger State. ‎He commended Governor Bago for demonstrating commitment to the rule of law by establishing the Judicial Commission of Inquiry to investigate the incident and ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were thoroughly examined. ‎Mu’azu assured that the Ministry of Justice would carefully study the report and advise the government on appropriate actions and the next steps to be taken. ‎ ‎ The post Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: Violence, Intimidation, Use Of Thugs May Discourage Voters, Amupitan Warns Political Parties
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has condemned violence associated with political campaigns, warning political parties and their supporters against actions capable of threatening peace and undermining the electoral process. Amupitan warned on Thursday as ‎ the Commission and security agencies meet to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 general election. ‎The INEC Chairman stressed the need for political actors to embrace issue-based campaigns, respect opposing views and conduct their political activities within the provisions of the law. Stressing that no political ambition is worth the blood of the citizens ‎He noted that political violence, intimidation and the use of thugs recently witnessed in some states during campaigns could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the democratic process. ‎ Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, and National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, at the meeting. ‎Prof Amupitan said that the commission is working closely with the office of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to identify flash points across the country. ‎He noted that election security remains a collective responsibility, requiring all relevant agencies to work together in addressing violence, intimidation and other activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections. Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu at the meeting ‎Amupitan further emphasised the need for security agencies to operate with professionalism, impartiality and respect for the rule of law, warning that no political interest should be allowed to compromise their constitutional responsibilities. ‎In attendance are the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, the Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, among others. ‎The Inspector-General of Police, in his welcoming address, emphasised the need for improved collaboration, intelligence sharing and coordinated security operations to address potential threats to the electoral process. Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, at the meeting.
